meaning: You have the same quality that was just mentioned about me.
example: You're very kind. — So are you.
note: Match the auxiliary: You look tired — So do you. You're tired — So are you. You are too also works after You're kind.
prompt: A friend says you are very kind. Return the same compliment.
transfer: Someone says you are a good listener. Tell them the same is true of them.
transferSample: So are you. You always listen carefully.

meaning: Are you doing anything interesting or do you have many plans?
example: Are you up to much this weekend?
note: A casual way to ask about plans. Not up to much means you have no major plans.
prompt: Ask a friend casually whether they have any plans this weekend.
transfer: Start a relaxed chat by asking whether a friend has plans tonight.
transferSample: Are you up to much tonight?

meaning: Tell me what your day or shift at work was like.
note: Use was for a finished shift. How's work going? asks about the current situation more generally.
prompt: Your friend has just finished a shift. Ask about their day.
transfer: Your partner worked late yesterday. Ask how that shift went.

meaning: Meet another person, usually by arrangement, to spend time together.
example: Do you want to meet up after work?
note: Meet up with someone names the other person. Meetup can be a noun for an organised gathering.
prompt: Invite a friend to spend time with you after work.
transfer: Arrange to see a former classmate when you visit their city.
transferSample: Let's meet up when I'm in town.

meaning: Choose between answering a question honestly and doing a challenge in a game.
example: It's your turn: truth or dare?
note: This is the name of a game as well as the question players ask. Players can decline uncomfortable questions or challenges.
prompt: It is a friend's turn in a game where they choose a truthful answer or a challenge. Ask them to choose.
transfer: Suggest this familiar question-and-challenge game for a party.
transferSample: Does anyone want to play truth or dare?

meaning: Persuade or pressure someone to come with you when they do not really want to.
example: My friends dragged me along to karaoke.
note: Often an exaggeration; it does not necessarily describe physically pulling someone. Drag someone to a place is also natural.
prompt: You did not want to sing, but your friends persuaded you to join them at karaoke. Describe what happened.
transfer: A sibling reluctantly persuaded you to attend a networking event.
transferSample: My sister dragged me along to a networking event.

meaning: Leave quietly and secretly so that other people do not notice.
example: We sneaked out before the speeches started.
note: Sneaked and snuck are both used as past forms. Snuck is especially common in informal English.
prompt: Describe leaving an event quietly before the speeches, without attracting attention.
transfer: A cat left through an open door while nobody noticed. Explain what happened.
transferSample: The cat snuck out while the door was open.

meaning: Agree to or cooperate with someone else's idea or plan.
example: I'll go along with your plan this time.
note: Go along with a plan means accept it. Join in means take part in an activity; it does not necessarily express agreement.
prompt: You are willing to accept a friend's proposed plan this time. Tell them.
transfer: A team chooses a different approach from yours. Say you will cooperate.
transferSample: I'm happy to go along with the team's decision.

meaning: Start taking part in an activity that other people are already doing.
example: Come and join in the game!
note: Join in an activity or join in with others. Join a club usually has no in.
prompt: Friends are playing a game. Invite someone watching to take part.
transfer: People are singing together. Describe beginning to sing with them.
transferSample: I joined in when I recognised the song.

meaning: An acknowledgement of the person who took a photograph.
example: Please include a photo credit when you post the picture.
note: Tagging the photographer links to their account; giving credit acknowledges their work. Credit does not replace permission to use a photo.
prompt: You took a photo for a friend. Ask them to acknowledge you when posting it.
transfer: Write a short caption acknowledging a fictional photographer named Alex.

expression: Are you available for a photo shoot?
meaning: Ask whether a photographer can take a booking for a photography session.
example: Are you available for a photo shoot next Saturday?
note: For pricing, ask Could you send me your rates? Add the type of shoot and date when making a real enquiry.
prompt: Ask a photographer whether they can take a booking next Saturday.
transfer: Enquire about a portrait session next month.
transferSample: Are you available for a portrait photo shoot next month?

meaning: Arrange in advance to use a service, place or facility at a particular time.
example: I'd like to make a booking for the rooftop barbecue area.
note: Make a reservation is similar. For an appointment, I'd like to book an appointment is natural and does not need will.
prompt: Ask reception to reserve the rooftop barbecue area.
transfer: Arrange a time to use a meeting room tomorrow afternoon.
transferSample: Can I make a booking for the meeting room tomorrow afternoon?

expression: I'd like to book an appointment
meaning: Politely ask to arrange a time to meet someone providing a service.
example: I'd like to book an appointment for Friday, please.
note: I'd means I would here. You can also say Can I book an appointment? There is no need to add will.
prompt: Politely ask a receptionist to arrange an appointment on Friday.
transfer: Ask a salon for an appointment next week.
transferSample: I'd like to book an appointment for next week, please.

meaning: Choose clothes and accessories that work well together for an occasion.
example: I'm putting an outfit together for the wedding.
note: Pick out an outfit focuses on choosing it. Lay out your clothes means arrange them ready to wear.
prompt: Explain that you are choosing coordinated clothes for a wedding.
transfer: A friend needs help choosing clothes for an interview. Offer help.
transferSample: I can help you put an outfit together for the interview.

meaning: Record moving images with a camera.
example: Can you film a short video for me?
note: Film is also a noun meaning a movie. Take a photo means capture a still image, while film describes recording video.
prompt: Ask someone to record a short video for you.
transfer: Describe recording a dance performance with a camera.

meaning: Express surprise about the length of time someone has just mentioned.
example: The queue took two hours. — That long?
note: Use That far? for distance and That much? for an amount or price. These short replies depend on the previous sentence.
prompt: A friend says they waited two hours. React with surprise about the duration.
transfer: Someone says a repair will take six weeks. React briefly.
transferSample: That long? I thought it would take a few days.

meaning: A form of poker in which players combine their two private cards with shared cards on the table.
example: They were talking about Texas hold'em.
note: Hold'em is a shortened spelling of hold them. This card teaches the game's name, not betting strategy.
prompt: Name the poker game with two private cards per player and shared cards on the table.
transfer: Ask a friend whether they know this type of poker.
transferSample: Do you know how Texas hold'em works?
